1) signal-based methods are superior to parametric methods for speech quality estimation; 2) the performance of signal-based methods is highly dependent on the quality and availability of reference speech data; and 3) parametric methods can be used to estimate the quality of a transmission channel when no reference speech data are available

the quality of a transmission channel can be estimated from a single speech signal measured at the channel output, and that the quality of the transmission channel is a linear function of the quality of the input signal.

1) the most important speech quality metric is the mean opinion score (MOS) of a large number of listeners; 2) the MOS is a nonlinear function of the speech signal; and 3) the most important parameters that determine the MOS are the speech signal-to-noise ratio (SNR), the signal distortion, and the signal delay.
